headline: New Agent Evidence Levels (AEL) standard grades AI agent actions for verifiable proof
summary: AEL introduces a graded scale (AEL-0 to AEL-4) and an open-source checker to verify AI agent actions, reducing reliance on vendor or operator trust.
details: Agent Evidence Levels (AEL) is a new open standard designed to grade the verifiable evidence an AI agent leaves behind. It addresses the critical question of how an outside party can know what an agent did without simply taking the word of the vendor or operator.

The standard runs from AEL-0 through AEL-4, with each level defining how much of an agent's actions and potential omissions can be verified by an external party. It ships with a runnable reference checker and a conformance corpus, allowing users to demonstrate a grade rather than merely asserting it.

AEL grades are cumulative, with a reproducibility suffix (R) indicating when a recorded decision can be re-derived from its inputs. However, no level claims to prove completeness against the party holding the signing keys, as a keyholder can always construct and sign a clean, but potentially incomplete, history.

The spec, reference checker, and conformance corpus are all public and open-source. The author intends to donate the standard to a neutral home once it gains traction, encouraging community feedback to identify and address any potential gaps in its claims.

How can you truly verify what your AI agent did without trusting the vendor? A new open standard provides a graded scale for verifiable evidence.

AEL grades are cumulative, with a reproducibility suffix (R) indicating when a recorded decision can be re-derived from its inputs. However, no level claims to prove completeness against the party holding the signing keys, as a keyholder can always construct and sign a clean, but potentially incomplete, history.
